PullRequest.Title: round up thinking labels
PullRequest.Body:
- Durations of 0 ms, 1 ms, and 999 ms will now display as 1s.
  - Durations of 1,001 ms will display as 2s, and 83,001 ms will display as 1m 24s.
- Updated unit tests in `chatThinkingContentPart.test.ts` and `chatListRenderer.test.ts` to reflect the new expected labels, including new test cases for 1 ms, 1,001 ms, and 83,001 ms.
- Added a note in the README.md to document the new rounding rule for reasoning duration labels.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or refresh a completed chat reasoning-duration label, including grouped reasoning rows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On initial rendering of completed reasoning, or after a changed reasoningDurationMs value is matched, the UI synchronously computes the label before setting title/text content. The diff adds Math.ceil, Math.max, division, and multiplication before the existing localization and elapsed-time formatting; no asynchronous work gates progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One computation per completed single-run title and per displayed unique reasoning source when timing changes. History/group size affects a pre-existing render loop, while the diff adds only O(1) work to each existing formatter invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs synchronously on the UI thread. Timing refreshes are coalesced by reasoningDurationSnapshots for unchanged values; grouped row formatting remains a serial loop over already-rendered parts, with no new task scheduling or parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Existing duration snapshots suppress unchanged timing updates, and the change neither introduces cache keys nor changes cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both call sites, the timing-update deduplication, the grouped-label loop, and the formatter implementation were inspected; the diff only changes constant-time arithmetic passed to the existing formatter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark was inspected, but the added work is a fixed number of primitive arithmetic operations per formatted label, so realistic duration values and chat history size do not create a new scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed label rounding adds negligible constant-time CPU work without new DOM geometry reads, retained state, allocation proportional to duration, or subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced the runtime formatter through construction, finalization, grouped-label refresh, and timing-update deduplication. Documentation and tests have no product runtime impact; the production change adds only bounded arithmetic to existing label formatting, so no performance finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
